approval.cost: No listing fee or review cost stated in the docs read
approval.trigger: Connectable integrations: no pre-approval gate to distribute. Once created, the integration gets a Community badge and 'will be available for external users to download' via your own site or a Deploy Button, but it does NOT appear in the public Marketplace. Public Marketplace listing is gated: at least 500 active installations (500 accounts), compliance with the review guidelines/approval checklist, then email integrations@vercel.com to request review. Native integrations are partner-gated from the start (provider signup, shared Slack channel, product form, final walkthrough call). Sign in with Vercel Apps: the docs describe no review or approval step at all.
approval.wait: No review duration stated anywhere in the docs read

blockers.detail: You cannot even request a public Marketplace listing for a connectable integration until you have 500 active installations. Distribution before that is your own site or a Deploy Button only, under a Community badge that signals 'not in the marketplace'.
blockers.howToClear: Plan your own distribution channel first; treat listing as a later milestone and instrument install counts from launch.
blockers.title: The 500-install wall

blockers.detail: An Integration's client ID/secret and a Sign in with Vercel App's client ID/secret are different objects in different consoles, with different endpoints (Apps authorize at vercel.com/oauth/authorize; integrations receive their code on the install Redirect URL). Using one where the other is expected fails.
blockers.howToClear: Decide which object you actually need (API access = Integration; identity = App) before writing any code.
blockers.title: Two credential systems to confuse

blockers.detail: Native integrations (products provisioned and billed through Vercel) require signing up as a native integration provider and coordinating with Vercel in a shared Slack channel. An agent cannot just create one.
blockers.howToClear: Start with the self-serve connectable flavor; pursue native only as a partnership.
blockers.title: Native is not self-serve

Sign in with Vercel 'App' (Team Settings > Apps; standard OAuth 2.0/OIDC identity client: openid required, profile, email, offline_access; identity-only today because token-carried API permissions are 'currently in private beta')
flavor.recommended: A connectable account Integration (Integrations Console), installed via Redirect URL + OAuth flow with console-declared API Scopes
flavor.why: Vercel has two OAuth-flavored objects that developers routinely confuse. The Integration is the one that grants API access to users' projects/teams: creating one assigns a client (integration) ID and secret, and you declare API Scopes per resource (deployment, project, project-env-vars, domain, team, user, integration-configuration, drains, billing) at None / Read / Read-Write. The Sign in with Vercel App is an identity client; for dependable programmatic API access today, the docs point you to the Integration model.

humanMust: Complete the long Create Integration form (legal developer name, EULA URL, Privacy Policy URL, listing media) and accept Vercel's terms
Email integrations@vercel.com for listing review once 500 active installs are reached
name: Vercel
nuances: Integration install codes are valid 30 minutes and single-use. The exchanged integration access token is described as 'long-lived', with no refresh token and no expiry documented.

Sign in with Vercel tokens are the opposite: access token lasts 1 hour, refresh token lasts 30 days and rotates on each use, and refresh requires the offline_access scope. Apps allow at most two active client secrets at a time (for rotation) and several client authentication methods (client_secret_basic/post, client_secret_jwt, private_key_jwt, oidc_token, none).

Ownership trap: if the integration's owner(s) leave the owning team, the integration is flagged disabled (API calls fail 403 integration_configuration_disabled, most webhooks pause); the team has 30 days to transfer ownership or the integration is deleted.

Scopes are set at the integration level in the console (None/Read/Read-Write per resource), not requested per authorize call; scope changes surface to installs via the integration-configuration.scope-change-confirmed webhook.
Install-UX gotchas: if your app sets Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy it must be unsafe-none or the Vercel dashboard cannot monitor the install popup; localhost redirect URLs are allowed for testing.

Sign-in access switch: an App can be restricted to members of the owning team; Vercel re-checks at authorize AND at token refresh, denying refreshes (access_denied) after a user leaves the team, though existing app sessions are not ended.
prerequisites: A Vercel team (integrations are created under a team)
The full listing packet up front: legal developer name, contact and support emails, logo (1:1, min 256px), EULA URL, Privacy Policy URL, documentation URL, feature media (1-8 images, 16:9, 1920x1080)
A Redirect URL endpoint that can exchange the install code and render the install UI

steps.detail: Dashboard: select team > Integrations > Integrations Console > Create. Complete the form in full: name, URL slug, developer (legal name), contact email (private), support email (public), short description, logo, category, website, documentation URL, EULA URL, Privacy Policy URL, overview, feature media, Redirect URL, API Scopes, optional webhook and configuration URLs; accept Vercel's terms to publish. You receive a client (integration) ID and secret.
steps.title: Create the Integration (long form)

steps.detail: Your Redirect URL endpoint must exchange the install code for a token, render the install UI in a popup, let users connect projects, and redirect back to Vercel on completion.
steps.title: Build the Redirect URL endpoint

steps.detail: POST api.vercel.com/v2/oauth/access_token, form-encoded, with client_id, client_secret, code, redirect_uri. The install code is valid 30 minutes and single-use. Response: access_token (described as long-lived; no refresh/expiry documented), installation_id, user_id, team_id (non-null team_id means installed on a team; append teamId to API calls).
steps.title: Exchange the install code

steps.detail: Distribute immediately via your own site or a Deploy Button under the Community badge. For a public Marketplace listing you need at least 500 active installations plus checklist compliance, then email integrations@vercel.com to request review.
steps.title: Distribute (Community now, Marketplace at 500 installs)

tagline: Two different OAuth objects hide under one brand: the Integration (API access, self-serve, Community distribution) and the Sign in with Vercel App (identity only, API permissions still private beta). The Marketplace won't review the Integration until it already has 500 active installs.

time.active: ~30-45 min dashboard form + ~half a day of install-endpoint work
time.total: Same day to distribute; Marketplace listing waits on 500 installs plus an unstated review duration
